description: SoundShape cross-modal mapping spec. Maps an emotion vector (category, valence, arousal) to a visual specification (shape, color, size, motion). Each channel's rule is grounded in published cross-modal correspondence research. Human-readable justification: docs/mapping_rationale.md. This file is the single source of truth, consumed by both backend/mapping/engine.py and frontend/src/lib/mapping.ts (the frontend copy is synced via scripts/sync_mapping_config.py).

shape.citation: Köhler (1929); Ramachandran & Hubbard (2001) — Bouba/Kiki effect: angular forms pair with harsh / high-arousal sounds; rounded, flowing forms pair with soft / low-arousal sounds.

color.citation: Hupka et al. (1997) — cross-cultural color-emotion associations: red=anger, blue=sadness, yellow=joy, consistent across six cultures. Russell (1980) — saturation scales with arousal; calmer states read as more muted.

size.citation: Russell (1980) arousal axis — perceptual salience scales with arousal; larger forms read as more intense / urgent.

motion.citation: Spence (2011) — crossmodal correspondences tutorial. Banse & Scherer (1996) — vocal instability (high arousal, jitter/shimmer) corresponds to agitated motion; low-arousal states to slow drift / settling.

rules.why: High arousal + negative valence (anger-like) → sharp, jittery agitation.
High arousal + non-negative valence (joy/surprise) → energetic pulsing.
Calm sadness → slow horizontal drifting, like a sigh.
Resignation → slow downward sink, an exhale.
